headline: Midterms flip Congress, Ottawa tables a budget, and Canada's job market weakens
summary: Democrats' midterm gains and the Iran conflict dominated the week abroad, while Ottawa's second budget and Ontario's $16.9B deficit shaped the domestic picture. Friday's jobs report showed Canada losing 4,700 jobs with unemployment at 6.7%.

top.headline: Iran war and Hormuz tensions
top.what: Trump has suggested the U.S. may have to go further against Iran after the midterms, keeping oil and markets volatile.
top.why: Energy prices drive Ontario gas and heating costs.

top.headline: Democrats flip Congress
top.what: Democrats won control of Congress; final counts are still firming up.
top.why: It reshapes U.S. trade and tariff policy that affects Canada.

top.headline: Ottawa's second budget projects $62.3B deficit
top.what: The federal budget adds about $142B in new spending and updates immigration levels.
top.why: It sets federal spending and housing programs affecting Ontarians.

top.headline: Canada loses 4,700 jobs; unemployment 6.7%
top.what: October job losses followed 68,000 in September and pushed unemployment to its highest since April.
top.why: It shapes Bank of Canada rate decisions and job prospects.

top.headline: Canada-U.S. trade talks continue
top.what: Talks continue while Democrats vow to repeal tariffs.
top.why: Tariffs hit Ontario manufacturing and prices.

top.headline: Ontario deficit swells to $16.9B
top.what: The province's fall statement delayed a balanced budget because of tariffs.
top.why: It affects provincial spending and services.

top.headline: Ontario students walk out over OSAP cuts
top.what: Thousands of students left class to protest student aid changes.
top.why: It affects tuition and living costs for students.

top.headline: Russian bombing of Ukraine aid centre kills 26
top.what: A strike on an aid centre killed at least 26 people.
top.why: The war continues to shape global energy and security.
